French champagne producers have received permission to increase alcohol content to 15%, above the usual 13% limit, following summer heatwaves.

in
Extreme temperatures and drought increased sugar levels in grapes, potentially raising alcohol levels during fermentation. The Champagne region also recorded its earliest harvest, with industry officials warning that such conditions could become normal within 10 to 15 years.
The Comité Champagne said only a small number of wines are expected to exceed the previous limit, potentially reaching 13.1% or 13.2% alcohol.
The exceptional increase applies only to the 2026 harvest, which began in early August following severe spring frosts and five summer heatwaves.
Champagne from this vintage is unlikely to reach consumers until 2028, as it must age for at least 15 months.

full_text:
Richmond came within 880 votes of electing a female mayor of colour.
Alexa Loo came within 880 votes of becoming the first woman elected to be Richmond’s mayor.
Not only that, but she would have been the first person of colour elected to the role as well.
Loo, a Chartered Professional Accountant and two-time Olympic athlete in snowboarding, says she’s not exactly sure what the future holds for her. Starting in 2014, she’s been a Richmond city councillor, which included membership on several committees and a role at Metro Vancouver. She was raised in Richmond and is a single mom of two sons, aged 13 and 14.
After a recent column I wrote noting that just two of the eight new Richmond city councillors are women, Carol Day and Laura Gillanders, down from three, Loo contacted me to talk about women in politics.
She tried to convince many women to run for office.
“I talked to a lot of women, and they just said, ‘Nope, I could never do that. I can't be in the limelight like that. I don't want to be criticized all the time,’” Loo said.
Women face comments about their appearance more often than men and comments online can be harsh, she said.
One of the challenges of sitting on council for the past several years was that many meetings are held at 4 p.m., exactly the time kids get home from school, Loo said. It’s not easy to get childcare for just a few hours a day, so that timing makes being on council tough for mothers.
“It’s about creating spaces that are welcoming for people. We over-silo our diversity, equity and inclusion instead of just thinking how do we make this work for the most people?” she said.
One thing Loo wanted to bring into City Hall, and which would have increased diverse representation, was real-time translation for meetings and presentations. This would make it more comfortable to anyone to present at City Hall in any language but would also allow City Hall to have control over translations, she said.
Turns out women lost a lot of representation in the recent B.C. provincial election.
Since 2020, women had made up a slight majority of MLAs in Victoria, but after this election, assuming preliminary results hold, women will only make up 39 per cent of the legislature, Shari Graydon, CEO of Informed Perspectives, wrote in a recent op-ed in the Vancouver Sun.
Research shows that diverse teams make stronger decisions.
Graydon notes some of the changes made in B.C. while women held a majority of seats: free menstrual products in schools, free birth control and self-testing at home for HPV.
I believe women should represent at least half of all seats on any government, given women make up half the population. Changes like these are less likely to happen if women aren’t in the room.
I came across a bizarre fact in my research for this column.
Until this election, Richmond has had just three mayors since 1973: Gil Blair (1973-1990), Greg Halsey-Brandt (1990-2001) and Malcolm Brodie (2001-2026). They all bear a remarkable similarity to each other and to newly elected Mayor Rob Howard.
Vancouver, in contrast, has had 10 mayors since 1973. None have been women, but the last two, Ken Sim and Pete Fry, are people of colour.
Richmond’s provincial representation by women was also reduced in the Oct. 24 election, from 50 per cent, or two of four MLAs, to 25 per cent.
Despite the challenges, Loo encourages women to enter politics.
“I think it's worth getting involved in a campaign and finding out what it's like,” she said. “Align yourself with people that are interesting to you or that you align with on a values basis and support them in their campaign. That's a really good way to find out how things are done.”
As far as her own future, she doesn’t rule out another run for mayor if the timing is right.
“My heart is in Richmond. I love Richmond, and I'd love to have served as mayor,” she said. “If an opportunity comes back again, and it makes sense for my family, then for sure.”

Total value of projects reaches an all-time high of Dh2.78 trillion in Abu Dhabi
- PUBLISHED: Sun 8 Nov 2026, 4:46 PM
The total value of active development projects in Abu Dhabi has surpassed $758.79 billion (Dh2.78 trillion) across various stages of planning, development, and construction, according to BNC Networks, a construction intelligence provider.
These include urban construction projects worth $221.56 billion, Oil and Gas projects with a combined investment worth $595.67 billion, Transport projects worth $238.01 billion, Industrial projects worth US151.36 billion and Utilities projects worth $130.29 billion, according to BNC Networks which tracks 2,168 projects in Abu Dhabi with a combined value of $475.41 billion.
The news comes as more than 4,000 property buyers, investors, real estate brokers, developers, asset managers and trade visitors are expected to participate at the International Real Estate and Investment Show (IREIS) 2026 that will be held at the Abu Dhabi National Exhibition Centre (ADNEC) from November 10 to 12, 2026, bringing together industry stakeholders to one of the UAE’s most prominent dedicated real estate sales exhibitions.
“Abu Dhabi is entering an exciting new chapter in its real estate journey. What we are witnessing is not simply the expansion of the property market, but a broader transformation of the emirate into a globally competitive destination for investment, business, living and innovation,” Arun Bose, Director of IREIS, said.
“Over the coming years, we anticipate continued growth driven by population expansion, economic diversification, major infrastructure investments and the development of world-class residential, commercial, hospitality and mixed-use destinations. Abu Dhabi’s appeal lies in its long-term vision, economic stability, quality of life and commitment to creating sustainable communities that respond to the needs of future generations.”
The emirate of Abu Dhabi recorded Dh95.8 billion through 21,416 registered home sales during the first 9 months (January to September) of 2026. Total real estate transaction value for the first nine months of 2026 reached Dh175.7 billion.
Residential supply in Abu Dhabi reaches approximately 409,000 units, with 71,000 additional units projected by 2030 and deliveries peaking in 2028. Around 7,562 to 8,000 residential units are scheduled for completion across 2026, with activity heavily back-loaded toward the second half of the year. As many as 233,000 active residential lease contracts were recorded across the emirate, with lease values reaching Dh9.3 billion in the first half of 2026.
Leading property developers and other stakeholders are joining IREIS 2026, as investor confidence strengthens in UAE’s real estate. Abu Dhabi Global Markets (ADGM) joins IREIS as its Official Knowledge Partner while Samana Developers, Aqaar and Al Rasikhoon Real Estate partners with IREIS as Gold Sponsor, De Sousa Holdings as Platinum Sponsor in addition to Silver Sponsors, Ellington Properties, Dugasta Properties, Zimaya Properties and Capstone Real Estate and Vertix Holding reaffirming commitment as Strategic Partner of IREIS 2026.
Alongside the exhibition, IREIS 2026 will feature a high-level conference bringing together government representatives, developers, financial institutions, economists and industry experts.
The market is also evolving in terms of investor expectations. Buyers and investors are becoming increasingly sophisticated, looking beyond property ownership towards long-term value, lifestyle, connectivity, sustainability and the overall quality of the communities in which they invest, he said.
“We believe the next phase of Abu Dhabi’s real estate growth will be defined by innovation, sustainability, smart urban development and greater international participation. The opportunities will extend beyond residential real estate to include commercial assets, hospitality, retail, industrial and logistics developments, as well as integrated investment opportunities,” Arun Bose says.

full_text:
Storm Bruna reached the Canary Islands during the night leading into Sunday. The AEMET weather stations reported the strongest gusts on the mountain peaks: 109 kilometres per hour at Roque de los Muchachos on La Palma, 107 in Izaña and 101 at the Parador in the Cañadas del Mount Teide on Tenerife. The Alto de Igualero station at the top of La Gomera recorded 96. Even down at La Palma airport, winds reached 80.
However, the heavy rain has not yet set in. By 6 am, the heaviest rainfall had been recorded on La Palma: 15.8 millimetres in San Andrés y Sauces, 12.2 millimetres each in El Paso and Fuencaliente, and 11 millimetres at the airport. On the other islands, rainfall remained at just a few millimetres; in Izaña, it was 5.2 millimetres.
Orange rain warning in effect on four islands until 6.00 pm
An orange alert for heavy rain is in force until 6.00 pm across the whole of Tenerife, as well as on La Palma, La Gomera and El Hierro. The AEMET is forecasting up to 25 millimetres in one hour, up to 30 on La Palma, and up to 100 millimetres in twelve hours. Most of the rain is likely to fall on the western and southern slopes, whilst on La Palma it will be more prevalent at medium altitudes. The weather service is not entirely certain: 40 to 70 per cent.
Gran Canaria is next at 12 noon. The summit, east, south and west will then be on orange alert until midnight, with up to 25 millimetres per hour and 80 millimetres in twelve hours possible there. In the north of the island, conditions warrant a yellow warning, as is the case on Lanzarote and Fuerteventura. Thunderstorms? A yellow warning is in place across all seven islands, although hail may also occur in the north of Gran Canaria.
More from Garafía and Vallehermoso:
And the wind won’t die down before midnight. La Palma and the north of Tenerife remain on orange alert, with gusts of 90 kilometres per hour, and over 100 on the mountain peaks. For La Gomera, El Hierro, the rest of Tenerife and Gran Canaria, the alert is yellow with winds of 70, although in the mountains of La Gomera they may reach 90 in places.
Tenerife has activated the island’s emergency plan
As reported by the EFE news agency on Saturday, Tenerife’s emergency plan has been in force since midnight. The first consequences have already been felt: the basketball match between La Laguna Tenerife and Joventut will take place this Sunday behind closed doors.
On a day like this, it’s best to steer clear of the Barrancos. If it’s raining heavily higher up, the water can quickly and frequently reach areas where the sun is still shining down below. Hiking on the peaks of Tenerife and La Palma isn’t a good idea in these gusts, nor is the drive up there. You can find out what the conditions are like for each island in the weather overview.
